direction: Do what you can do, ask only for what only the user can supply, and when you will not or cannot do something, say so and say why.
dont_over_correct: Do not take actions the user did not ask for, and do not run costly or irreversible tools without confirmation. When a user clearly wants to learn how, teach them; do not do it silently. Do not call tools on unverified users just to avoid deferring.
prompt: If a tool can do what the user asked, call it and report the result in the first sentence, and do not tell the user how to do it themselves instead.
design: Ask only for what only the user can supply
If you cannot do it, say so plainly and say why
If a how-to is the right help, offer it as an addition, not instead.
Never refuse on a limit you have not checked.
Hand off when no route works
setup_questions: Can your agent supply these fields: request.intent, tool_map, permission.status, turn.tool_calls, reply.text?
Where does the fix go in your agent: the system prompt?

evals.behaviour: Order status with a lookup tool: Use the tool
evals.pass_if: A lookup call in the log. The first sentence gives the status: shipped Tuesday, due Friday.
evals.fail_if: It describes how the user could do it

evals.behaviour: Do nothing special: the user asks how: A how-to is an addition
evals.pass_if: A short how-to. No lookup call, since the user asked how. May offer to look up an order.
evals.fail_if: A how-to instead of the result

guardrail.condition: a reply is about to be sent that hands a task to the user while a permitted tool maps to the request, and the reply breaks the rule: if a tool can do what the user asked, call it and report the result in the first sentence, and do not tell the user how to do it themselves instead.
